thread:
alice.j: Quick heads-up — I opened a PR to add a new `gpu-micro` nodepool for low-latency small-inference jobs. Can folks do a config sanity check before I merge? PR: https://git.redwood/example/pr/412

ben_park: Nice. What are you thinking for instance types and capacity plan? spot-only or mixed?

alice.j: Proposal in the PR: mixed pool — prefer g5-small (4GB-ish GPU) equiv if available, otherwise fallback to standard g4/rtx small. Reserve 2 nodes as capacity-reservation for predictability, rest can be spot.

carlos_ops: A couple quick calls out:
- If we do mixed (reserved + spot) we need a robust eviction/fallback policy on the service side.
- We should taint the pool `gpu=micro:NoSchedule` so only inference pods with tolerations land there.
- Make sure the nodepool IAM has access to the KMS key for mounting the GPU driver secret (we use CSI + KMS unwrap).

alice.j: Yep on taint. I added toleration example in the PR docs. For the driver secret, I referenced `secret/gpu-drivers-prod` (no secrets in PR) and attached nodepool sa `infra-gpu-node` in terraform.

dana_ml: Also check CUDA runtime. Some models need >=11.8. Are we pinning a node image with driver/operator? If not, we'll get driver mismatch flakes.

ben_park: Good point. We should use the GPU Operator + node image combo we validated in sandbox. Might be worth adding a `nodeSelector` label `gpu-runtime: cuda11_8` on the pool so rollout is explicit.

carlos_ops: Terraform nit: don't use inline `preemptible` flag without a fallback pool in the rollout. If a bunch of pods are evicted at once, we need automatic fallback to `cpu-inference` or to the reserved nodes. Add a `pod disruption budget` and an HPA-aware scaling plan.

alice.j: I'll add PDB + HPA note. Also thinking of adding `maxSurge: 1` for rolling updates on deployments targeting that pool.

ben_park: Sharing a small TF snippet that worked in staging for mixed reservation:
```hcl
resource "google_compute_reservation" "gpu_micro" {
  name         = "res-gpu-micro"
  zone         = var.zone
  machine_type = "n1-standard-4"
  count        = 2
  specific_reservation {  # narrow to GPU SKU
    instance_properties { /* ... */ }
  }
}

resource "google_container_node_pool" "gpu_micro" {
  name       = "gpu-micro"
  cluster    = var.cluster
  autoscaling { min_node_count = 2; max_node_count = 10 }
  node_config {
    taint { key = "gpu"; value = "micro"; effect = "NO_SCHEDULE" }
    labels = { "gpu-runtime" = "cuda11_8" }
    service_account = "infra-gpu-node@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
  }
}
```

carlos_ops: That looks fine but adapt to whatever cloud we're on. Also ensure the nodepool creation waits for the reservation attachment (we had transient scheduling failures if not attached).

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Reminder — nodepool creation will trigger a cluster update. Expected downtime: none, but API rate limits may slow control-plane ops.

alice.j: Thanks. Action items for me:
- Add PDB + HPA guidance to the PR
- Pin node image to verified GPU operator + CUDA 11.8 and label the pool
- Ensure nodepool SA has KMS unwrap permission for `secret/gpu-drivers-prod`
- Add fallback runbook for large-scale spot eviction
I'll update the PR in ~30m.

dana_ml: If you can add a short smoke test (small model load + token gen) to the rollout CI that runs against the reserved nodes, that will catch driver mismatches early.

alice.j: Good call — will add. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ben_park: LGTM once those updates are in.

alice.j: Updated PR with the changes, thanks all — https://git.redwood/example/pr/412 — merging in 10m if no objections.

carlos_ops: No objections from infra side.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: merge queued by alice.j. CI checks running.
